What is RAM?

Tech Compass · Updated 2026-10-19

IN THIS GUIDE

The quick answerThink of it as your workbenchWhat happens when memory fills up?Check before you upgradeDoes more RAM mean more storage?Further reading
THE QUICK ANSWER

RAM is your computer’s short-term working memory. It holds the information your apps are using right now. Storage keeps your files when the power is off; RAM does not.

Think of it as your workbench

Your storage is the cupboard where you keep everything. RAM is the workbench where you spread out the things you are using. A bigger workbench lets you work on more things at once, but it does not make every individual tool faster.

What happens when memory fills up?

Your operating system can move less-active data to storage to free up RAM. This is slower than accessing RAM directly. Switching between apps may feel sluggish, especially when several demanding programs are open. A slow computer can have other causes, so check memory use before buying an upgrade.

Check before you upgrade

On Windows, open Task Manager and choose Performance, then Memory. On macOS, open Activity Monitor and look at Memory Pressure. Check this while doing your usual work. Consult your device manual before buying: some memory is soldered in place, and different DDR generations are not interchangeable.

Does more RAM mean more storage?

No. Adding RAM does not give you more room for saved photos or games. You need more storage for that. The right memory capacity depends on the apps you use and their requirements.

Why is my computer running slowly?

A slow computer may be short of memory or storage space, busy with background work, or getting too hot. Start by finding what is busy instead of installing a cleaner app.

SSD vs. HDD: what’s the difference?

An SSD stores data in flash memory. An HDD stores it on spinning magnetic platters. Both keep files without power, but SSDs usually access data much faster.

What does a CPU actually do?

The CPU executes the instructions that make software work. It handles calculations, decisions, and coordination across the computer.
